domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
attributes: reversesRequestId: string | null  // NEW — null for every ordinary request; set only on a reversal row, pointing at the original APPROVED request it reverses
domain_entities.purpose: A single application by an employee for a span of leave of one type, moving through an approval lifecycle. GP-008 makes a completed approval immutable: an APPROVED row is never mutated, and cancelling it produces a NEW LeaveRequest row that references it. The canonical shape is a cross-module data contract and must not gain, lose, or rename any field without a matching repository/schema change.
lifecycle_states: CANCELLED_IN_PLACE (derived: status = CANCELLED AND reversesRequestId = null)
CANCELLED_REVERSAL (derived: status = CANCELLED AND reversesRequestId != null)

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestReversal
attributes: reversalRequestId: string  // id of the NEW CANCELLED row
originalRequestId: string  // id of the untouched APPROVED row (reversalRequestId.reversesRequestId)
employeeId: string  // copied from the original
leaveTypeCode: LeaveTypeCode  // copied from the original
startDate: Date  // copied from the original
endDate: Date  // copied from the original
requestedDays: number  // copied verbatim from the original, never re-derived
releasedDays: number  // equals requestedDays; the amount returned to the balance exactly once
releasedFrom: 'PENDING' | 'USED' | 'NONE'  // SUBMITTED -> PENDING, APPROVED -> USED, DRAFT -> NONE
actorId: string  // cancelledBy on the reversal row
occurredAt: Date  // cancelledAt on the reversal row
domain_entities.purpose: Derived domain concept (no table of its own) describing the two-row representation of a cancelled-after-approval leave: the untouched original APPROVED LeaveRequest plus the NEW CANCELLED LeaveRequest whose reversesRequestId points at it. It exists so the domain has one named place to state the immutability, uniqueness and release-once invariants that span the two rows.
lifecycle_states: CREATED (the reversal row is inserted and the balance released in one transaction)
TERMINAL (a reversal row is itself immutable: it can never be submitted, approved, rejected or cancelled again)

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
attributes: available: number  // computed = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays; never persisted
domain_entities.purpose: The per-employee, per-leave-type, per-accrual-period reservation ledger. Unchanged by this feature except that the release triggered by a reversal must happen exactly once and in the same transaction as the reversal insert. available is computed, never persisted.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
attributes: action: AuditAction  // CANCEL for both cancellation paths
entityId: string  // the mutated row (in-place) or the NEW reversal row (reversal)
beforeState: unknown | null  // the original APPROVED LeaveRequest for a reversal
afterState: unknown | null  // the NEW CANCELLED LeaveRequest for a reversal
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable record of every state-changing operation (GP-002). A cancellation still writes exactly one CANCEL entry; for a reversal the entry is anchored on the NEW row and carries the original APPROVED row as beforeState, so the untouched original leaves no UPDATE trail.

domain_entities.name: Notification
attributes: recipientId: string  // the original request's employeeId
relatedEntityId: string | null  // the NEW reversal row id
domain_entities.purpose: Synchronous in-app notice to the requester that their leave was cancelled. Unchanged by this feature; the reversal path sends the same single cancellation notification as the in-place path, addressed to the original request's employeeId.

business_rules: GP-008 immutability: once a LeaveRequest reaches APPROVED, its status, approverId, approvalComment and decidedAt are immutable. No operation may UPDATE those fields on an APPROVED row. Cancelling an APPROVED request must not mutate it in any way (including cancelledBy/cancelledAt, which stay null on the original). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest APPROVED state; every state-changing operation on leave requests appears, not only here]

Reversal representation: cancelling an APPROVED LeaveRequest inserts a NEW LeaveRequest row with status CANCELLED, cancelledBy = actor.id, cancelledAt = now, and reversesRequestId = the original request's id. The original row is left byte-identical. The reversal row copies employeeId, leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate and requestedDays verbatim from the original; requestedDays is copied, never re-derived from the dates. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest reversal construction; requestedDays concept appears, not only here]

In-place cancellation is preserved for non-completed states: cancelling a DRAFT or SUBMITTED request mutates that same row to CANCELLED (cancelledBy/cancelledAt set, reversesRequestId stays null). No completed approval exists in those states, so GP-008 does not apply and no new row is created. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest DRAFT/SUBMITTED cancellation appears, not only here]

Balance release happens exactly once per cancellation, in the same transaction as the status change or reversal insert: DRAFT releases nothing (no balance read or write); SUBMITTED releases the full requestedDays from pendingDays; APPROVED releases the full requestedDays from usedDays (no pro-rating). A reversal must not double-release (the original APPROVED row is never re-processed) and must not skip the release. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance pendingDays/usedDays; cancellation and reversal paths appears, not only here]

At most one reversal may exist per original request: reversesRequestId is unique among non-null values, so a second cancellation attempt against an already-reversed APPROVED request is rejected with ConflictError rather than inserting a second CANCELLED row or releasing the balance twice. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest.reversesRequestId uniqueness; cancellation idempotency appears, not only here]

A reversal row is terminal: a LeaveRequest whose reversesRequestId is non-null can never be submitted, approved, rejected or cancelled again. Cancellation authorization and the timing guard are evaluated against the ORIGINAL request's status and startDate, never against the reversal row. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest reversal row; cancel/submit/approve/reject guards appears, not only here]

Cancellation authorization is unchanged by this feature: the owner may cancel their own DRAFT or SUBMITTED request; an APPROVED request may be cancelled only by the requester's direct manager (employee.managerId === actor.id) or an ADMIN (exempt from the direct-manager check). All other combinations throw ForbiddenError. The timing guard is also unchanged: cancellation is blocked once startDate <= today (UTC day comparison) with ConflictError. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation authorization and timing appears, not only here]

Exactly one AuditLog entry with action CANCEL is written per cancellation (GP-002). For a reversal the entry's entityId is the NEW reversal row id, beforeState is the original APPROVED LeaveRequest and afterState is the NEW CANCELLED LeaveRequest; no audit entry is written against the untouched original. Exactly one cancellation Notification is sent to the original request's employeeId, with relatedEntityId = the reversal row id. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever AuditLog and Notification side effects of cancellation appears, not only here]

The reversal insert, the balance release, the audit write and the notification insert all occur inside a single IUnitOfWork.withTransaction unit of work, with the PoolClient threaded to every participating repository/service call; the balance row is read with forUpdate = true before it is written. A partial reversal (row inserted without release, or release without row) is never observable. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Cancellation transaction boundary appears, not only here]

Wire honesty: because a cancelled-after-approval request is represented by two rows, the LeaveRequest read model exposes reversesRequestId so a client can distinguish the untouched original (status APPROVED, reversesRequestId null) from the reversal (status CANCELLED, reversesRequestId set). A client must not infer "cancelled" from status alone when reversesRequestId is null on an APPROVED row. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest read model / GET /leaves and GET /leaves/:id appears, not only here]

Role-scoped visibility applies identically to reversal rows: the reversal row carries the original's employeeId, so EMPLOYEE sees it as their own, MANAGER sees it for direct reports, ADMIN sees all. An unauthorized single-read of a reversal row returns the same 404 as a nonexistent id. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest visibility scoping appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## GP-008 reversal — domain slice

### Entities touched
- **LeaveRequest** — gains one nullable field, `reversesRequestId: string | null` (null for every ordinary request; set only on a reversal row). Canonical shape goes from 14 to 15 fields; `CreateLeaveRequestInput = Omit<LeaveRequest,'id'>` therefore also gains it (ordinary creates supply `null`). `UpdateLeaveRequestDto` must NOT gain `reversesRequestId` — a reversal row's link is set at insert and is immutable thereafter.
- **LeaveRequestReversal** — new *derived* concept (no table): the two-row representation of a cancelled-after-approval leave (untouched original + new CANCELLED row). It is the named home for the cross-row invariants (immutability, uniqueness, release-once).
- **LeaveBalance**, **AuditLog**, **Notification** — unchanged in shape; only their participation in the reversal transaction is specified.

### Lifecycle states introduced (for architectureMdUpdate)
Existing canonical states are unchanged: LeaveRequest DRAFT | SUBMITTED | APPROVED | REJECTED | CANCELLED; LeaveBalance OPEN | CLOSED; LeavePolicy DRAFT | ACTIVE | SUPERSEDED; Employee ACTIVE | TERMINATED | ON_LEAVE; AuditLog RECORDED; Notification PENDING | SENT | READ | ARCHIVED; LeaveType static.

New states to fold in:
1. **LeaveRequest.CANCELLED_IN_PLACE** — derived, not stored: `status = CANCELLED AND reversesRequestId = null`. Produced by cancelling a DRAFT or SUBMITTED request; the same row is mutated.
2. **LeaveRequest.CANCELLED_REVERSAL** — derived, not stored: `status = CANCELLED AND reversesRequestId != null`. Produced by cancelling an APPROVED request; a NEW row, the original left APPROVED.
3. **LeaveRequestReversal.CREATED** — the reversal row is inserted and the balance released in one transaction.
4. **LeaveRequestReversal.TERMINAL** — a reversal row is itself immutable and can never be submitted, approved, rejected or cancelled again.

No new *stored* enum member is added to `LeaveStatus`; the two CANCELLED variants are discriminated by `reversesRequestId`, which is why that field must be on the read model.

### Transition table (named)
- `cancelDraftInPlace`: DRAFT → CANCELLED (same row; no balance touch; reversesRequestId stays null).
- `cancelSubmittedInPlace`: SUBMITTED → CANCELLED (same row; pendingDays -= requestedDays; reversesRequestId stays null).
- `cancelApprovedByReversal`: APPROVED → (original unchanged) + insert CANCELLED reversal row with reversesRequestId = original.id; usedDays -= requestedDays.
- `reversalTerminal`: reversal row → no further transitions.

### Boundary semantics decided (broad, not narrow)
- **requestedDays on a reversal row is COPIED verbatim from the original, never re-derived.** This is the BR-001 guard for this feature: the release path consumes the same count the original reserved, so re-deriving it from dates would be a second, divergent derivation of the canonical inclusive day count. The canonical derivation itself remains `requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1` inclusive whole-day UTC via the single shared helper.
- **Release amount = the original's requestedDays, full, no pro-rating**, on both the in-place SUBMITTED path (pendingDays) and the reversal path (usedDays). The existing timing guard (`startDate <= today` → ConflictError) is what makes pro-rating unnecessary and is unchanged.
- **Release exactly once**: the original APPROVED row is never re-processed, and `reversesRequestId` is unique among non-null values, so a second cancel attempt on an already-reversed request is a ConflictError rather than a second row or a second release.
- **Authorization and timing are evaluated against the ORIGINAL request**, never against the reversal row.

### Cross-entity rules
- One CANCEL AuditLog per cancellation; for a reversal it is anchored on the NEW row (entityId = reversal id, beforeState = original APPROVED, afterState = new CANCELLED) so the untouched original leaves no UPDATE trail.
- One cancellation Notification to the original's employeeId, relatedEntityId = reversal row id.
- Reversal insert + balance release + audit + notification are one `IUnitOfWork.withTransaction` unit of work, balance read with `forUpdate = true`.
- Role-scoped visibility applies identically to reversal rows (they carry the original's employeeId); unauthorized single-read still returns the same 404 as a nonexistent id.

### Consistency notes / flags
- The web client's `getAvailableLeaveActions(status, role, isOwner)` currently treats `status === CANCELLED` as terminal and `APPROVED` as non-cancellable for the owner. After this change an APPROVED request *is* cancellable by a manager/ADMIN, and the original row keeps reading APPROVED after reversal — the client must key off `reversesRequestId`, not status alone. Flagged for the application architect; not re-decided here.
- `docs/DOMAIN.md` remains stale/non-canonical; this slice extends `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and does not contradict it.
- Pre-existing unresolved items (no controller layer; `LeavePolicyStatus` module-local; `notifications.status` default `'unread'` outside `NotificationStatus`; `approvalComment`/`submittedAt` never populated) are untouched by this feature and remain open.

open_questions.question: Should reversal rows (status CANCELLED, reversesRequestId set) appear in the default GET /leaves result set, or be excluded/hidden behind an explicit flag?
open_questions.impact: A cancelled-after-approval leave now yields two rows for one business event. If reversal rows are returned by default, list counts, dashboards and any client-side aggregation double-count the leave; if they are hidden, a client cannot see that the cancellation happened without a second call. The choice also determines whether status=CANCELLED filtering returns reversal rows, in-place cancellations, or both.
candidate_options: Return both rows by default; clients distinguish via reversesRequestId (current read model)
Exclude reversal rows from the default list; expose them only via an explicit includeReversals=true query param
Return both rows but add a derived isReversal boolean to the read model so clients need not interpret reversesRequestId

open_questions.question: Should the reversal row copy approverId, approvalComment and decidedAt from the original APPROVED request, or leave them null?
open_questions.impact: The reversal row is a CANCELLED request that was never itself approved, so null is semantically clean; but copying them preserves the approval provenance on the row a client actually sees when filtering by CANCELLED. This affects read-model fidelity and whether a client can render "approved by X, then cancelled by Y" from one row.
candidate_options: Leave approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt null on the reversal row; provenance is reachable only by following reversesRequestId
Copy approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt verbatim from the original onto the reversal row
Copy approverId and decidedAt only (provenance), leave approvalComment null

open_questions.question: Does the untouched original APPROVED row still occupy its date range for overlap/duplicate-leave detection after it has been reversed?
open_questions.impact: The balance was released, so the employee has the days back, but the original row still reads APPROVED with the same startDate/endDate. If any future overlap check (or a client-side "already on leave" view) reads APPROVED rows, a reversed leave will still block the same dates; if it reads only non-reversed rows, the dates are free. No overlap check exists today, so this is a latent boundary that must be decided before one is added.
candidate_options: A reversed original no longer occupies its dates: overlap checks must exclude APPROVED rows that have a reversal row pointing at them
The original APPROVED row always occupies its dates; reversal only affects the balance, never date occupancy
Defer: no overlap check exists, so record the rule only when such a check is introduced
